chapter: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
title: Roy Porter and the cymbal stand
summary: Roy Porter replaces the older drummer and turns Edwards's music stand into a cymbal stand.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: But anyway, back to Howard McGhee's thing, we had it going pretty good. And Monk was kind of an elder fellow. He was a nice drummer, but he just wasn't into this thing that we were doing. It was a little fast for him, you know. So while we were at the Downbeat, Howard brought in Roy Porter, and he could play the tempos very good.

I'd like to mention something here about Roy Porter. While we were at the Downbeat Club, I had a music stand that he asked me if he could have. And he had an idea about something he wanted to do with this music stand. So Roy, I let him have it, and he took this music stand and he made a cymbal stand. And about six months later, the drum companies came out with cymbal stands -- and they've been a big seller ever since.
That's right. Until this day. Now, he is the one that started that, Roy Porter.
'45. This was 1945, somewhere round about June.
